newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss parliament approves Holocaust probe.
newsitem.headline: Swiss parliament approves Holocaust probe.

text.p: Switzerland's parliament gave final approval on Wednesday for a sweeping study of Swiss financial dealings with Nazi Germany and the fate of Jewish wealth stashed in Swiss banks during the Holocaust.

The government decree creates a panel of independent historians and financial and legal experts empowered to lift tight banking secrecy rules for a historical accounting of Swiss commerce with Nazi Germany.
Swiss purchases of Nazi gold were a crucial source of funds to finance the German war effort.

The panel will also review how much wealth was deposited with Swiss banks and other finance companies by Jews and other victims of Nazi persecution and whether the Swiss have done enough to identify the lost assets of those killed in the Holocaust.
The commission, expected to start work early next year, will have full access to bank archives from the war era, but bank secrecy will not be lifted from modern accounts.

The decree follows accusations by foreign critics that Switzerland could still be hoarding Nazi gold or holding millions of dollars in dormant assets of people who perished during Hitler's reign of terror.
